JUDGMENT

This appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (the Act) has been filed by the claim petitioner in O.P.(MV) No.218 of 2016 on the file of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal,
Mavelikara, (the Tribunal), aggrieved by the amount of compensation granted by Award dated 21/12/2019.
The sole respondent herein is the third respondent/insurer in the petition.
In this appeal, the parties and the documents will be referred to as described in the original petition.

2. According to the claim petitioner, on 30/09/2014 at about 07:30 p.m., while he was riding motorcycle bearing registration No.KL-29F-6499 through Thrikkunnappuzha-Thottappally public road and when he reached near Thrikkunnappuzha petrol pump in Pallippattu muri, autorickshaw bearing registration No.KL-29D-9711 driven by the first respondent in a rash and negligent manner,
knocked him down, as a result of which he sustained grievous injuries.
3. The first respondent/driver, the second respondent/owner and the third respondent/insurer remained ex parte.
4. Before the Tribunal, no oral evidence was adduced by either side.
Exts. A1
to A24 and X1 were marked on the side of the claim petitioner.
No documentary evidence was produced by the respondents.

6. The Tribunal on consideration of the documentary evidence and after hearing both sides, found negligence on the part of the first respondent/driver of the offending autorickshaw resulting in the incident and hence awarded an amount of 1,42,076/- together with interest @ 8% per annum from the date of petition till realisation along with proportionate costs.
Aggrieved by the Award, the claim petitioner has come up in appeal.
7. The only point that arises for consideration in this appeal is whether there is any infirmity in the findings of the Tribunal calling for an interference by this Court.
8. Heard both sides.

sentences.text: The award of compensation by the Tribunal under the following heads is challenged by the claim petitioner- 2025
Notional income
It is submitted by the learned counsel for the claim petitioner that the latter, a coolie, was earning 12,000/- per month.

However, the Tribunal fixed the notional income at 4,000/- which is quite low going by the dictum in Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Co. Ltd, (2011) 13 SCC 236.
9.1.

entities.text: Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Co. Ltd, (2011) 13 SCC 236
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the light of the dictum in Ramachandrappa (Supra), the notional income is fixed as 9,500/-.
Bystander expenses 10.
The materials on record show that he was hospitalized for a period of 40 days.
The accident took place on 30/09/2014.
Hence, he can be awarded compensation at the rate of 350/- per day for a period of 40 days, that is, 350/-x40 days= 14,000/-.
Pain and suffering 11.

The materials on record show that the claim petitioner sustained the following injuries:
"1. Lacerated wound right knee.
2. Type I open fracture femur, supra condylar right."
2025
He underwent two surgeries.
Therefore, taking into account the injury sustained, I find that an amount of 30,000/- as claimed would be just and reasonable under this head.
Loss of amenities 12.
In the facts and circumstances of the case, an amount of 30,000/- as claimed would be just and reasonable.

In the result, the appeal is allowed by enhancing the compensation by a further amount of 1,73,792/- (total compensation =3,15,868/- that is, 1,42,076/- granted by the Tribunal + 1,73,792/-
granted in appeal) with interest at the rate of 8% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realization and proportionate costs.
The third respondent/insurer is directed to deposit the compensation with interest and costs before the Tribunal within a period of 60 days from the date of receipt of a copy of the judgment.

On deposit of the compensation amount, the Tribunal shall disburse the amount to the claim petitioner at the earliest in accordance with law after making deductions, if any.
